findings.actual_primary_claim: The required exact+7/8/.28logT Cor1 is in The mean square of the error term in the prime number theorem (2008.06140v1PDFp4, JNT238(2022)p743). Accurate-estimation is a different2009.13791 paper and refers to that antecedent.
findings.trigger_and_impact: Wrong title conflates two real primary papers. The numeric bound is genuinely present in the linked2008 paper, so this is a citation identity repair, not a false zero-count theorem.

findings.Lean_Blueprint: RHSmoothingInputs.box_explicit_formula uses exact PsiSmoothing.trivial and log2pi. BOX_PNT_PROOF says integrate by parts againstDGM Psi1.
findings.actual_primary_claim: DGM1503.05403v2PDFp2 states exact Perron integral and Psi1=x^2/2-sumx^(rho+1)/[rho(rho+1)]-xr+rprime+R1(x), with|R1|<=.6/x; that display does not itself identifyr or differentiateR1.
findings.flawed_fragment: The exact trivial term -log(1-t^-2)/2 is asserted without displaying the recovery from boundedR1.
findings.trigger_and_impact: A bound on a remainder alone does not justify its derivative. The exact averaged explicit identity needs a classical residue expansion, rather than differentiating the.6/x inequality. No arithmetic bound is disproved.
findings.recoverable_derivation: From the displayed Perron integrand, pole1 givesx^2/2, eachrho gives-x^(rho+1)/[rho(rho+1)], pole0 gives-x log2pi, pole-1 contributes a constant, and simple trivialzero-2n gives-x^(1-2n)/[2n(2n-1)]. ThusR1 equals that negative uniformly convergent series forx>1; its derivative is sumx^-2n/(2n)=-.5log(1-x^-2), uniformly onx>=a>1. Then integration by parts gives the actual log-average formula.
findings.repair_requested: Add exact residue series and local uniform convergence argument to written proof, with source trace; do not upgrade formal status.
